chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Akhī Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He said regarding a man from whom something like a pumpkin seed comes out: wudu (ablution) is upon him.
So the proper way concerning it is that we interpret it to mean when it is smeared with feces and is not clean; and that which indicates this distinction is what follows.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for acts such as salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَبِّ الْقَرْعِ: a pumpkin seed; used here as a comparison for size or appearance
key_terms.يَخْرُجُ: comes out or exits from the body

ai.seo_question: Does the خروج of a worm or seed-like substance invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report discusses a legal ruling on wudu (ablution) when something resembling a pumpkin seed exits a person. The appended explanation clarifies that the ruling is to be understood in the case where it is soiled with feces and not clean, indicating a juristic distinction in ritual purity.
